display.purpose: Panel titles, the AGIS wordmark, totals, the stamp figure, the cash input and checkout-path button text. The larger of the two sizes.

compact.purpose: Everything else: body, labels, rows, chips, nav text. Rank by weight 400 / 600 / 700, never by another size.

label.purpose: The stamp's own word only (RATE, RATE LOCKED, STALE). The single uppercase device in the system.

motion.name: roll-in
motion.purpose: A changed digit on the live rate stamp rolls in from translateY(-0.55em); unchanged digits stay still.

motion.name: stamp-strike
motion.purpose: The locked stamp strikes the receipt on mount: scale 1.4 → 0.97 → 1 with rotation -5° → -2°. Both motions are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
Every screen is the carbon-copy weigh slip a Thai gold shop already hands across the counter. White slip panels sit on a pale gold-paper ground, the chrome (top bar, buttons, selected rows) is matte brass, and the one thing allowed to be loud is the live gold rate, struck onto the page as a red rubber stamp. Money lives in a single right-aligned tabular column; every price on screen visibly descends from the stamped rate. The world refuses both the category's white-cards-plus-one-accent shell and the dark luxury-boutique opposite: it is a working document, legible at arm's length under shop light, not a brand moment.

The system is flat by doctrine and quiet by construction. There are no shadows, no gradients and no ruled lines between rows; the only rules in the interface sit under a table header and above a total, and the dashed line above a receipt footer is a perforation in the paper, not a shelf. Type comes in exactly two sizes (compact and display) and ranks everything else by weight; the single uppercase word in the system is the stamp's own label. The face is Noto Sans with Noto Sans Thai, self-hosted at 400/600/700 with tabular figures, because the layout is designed for bilingual Thai/English even though it ships English strings today.

Every screen is built in this world: the cashier flow (catalog, bag and receipt, payment type, PromptPay/cash dialog, thank-you and printed slip), the manager editor (`src/pages/editorMenu.tsx`, `src/components/editorSide/*`), the auth pages (`LoginPage`, `RegisterPage`, `src/components/Authentication/*`) and `storeProfile`; the editor is the back of the same counter, with the same brass bar, slip rows and live price per piece. "AGIS" is a typographic wordmark standing in for a logo that does not exist yet; the ASIS SVG in `src/assets` is an upstream placeholder and is not part of the system.
keyCharacteristics: Gold-paper ground, white slip panels with a 1px brass-tinted edge and 6px corners
Brass chrome: a 64px brass-700 top bar, brass-700 action buttons, brass-100 selected rows and tags
One red rubber stamp for the live rate (3px double border, rolling digits, strikes the receipt at -2°)
Two type sizes only; rank by weight (400 / 600 / 700), never by a third size
One money column (7rem, right-aligned, tabular) on screen and on paper; prices in brass-800
No shadows, no gradients, no row rules; rules only under table headers and above totals
Lucide outline icons, 16–26px inline, 48px pictograms for payment types

rules.name: The Brass Carries Rule
rules.body: Brass carries the shell and the actions; red belongs to the stamp and to errors; green belongs to success and change. Nothing else on screen is coloured for emphasis. Attention is earned by weight or by the display size, not by a new hue.

rules.name: The Price Deep, Action Mid Rule
rules.body: Prices are bold brass-800 text; actions are white text on brass-700 fill. The two never swap, so a customer can tell a number from a tap target at a glance.

rules.name: The One Scheme Colour Rule
rules.body: Thai QR Navy appears only in the PromptPay dialog header, behind the scheme's own logo. Any other navy is a mistake.

rules.name: The Two Sizes Rule
rules.body: `--text-compact` (0.9375rem) and `--text-display` (1.75rem) are the only font sizes. A new element picks one and ranks by weight; it does not introduce 0.75rem, 1.125rem or any clamp.

rules.name: The One Money Column Rule
rules.body: Every amount on a receipt-like surface sits in `MONEY_COL` (`src/lib/gold.ts`): 7rem wide, right-aligned, tabular. Prices on cards and in dialogs are right-aligned and tabular even where the column is implicit. Money is always `thb()`: `฿` + grouped thousands + two decimals; gold is always `describeGold()`: `15.244 g · 96.5%`.

rules.name: The Stamp Owns Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is not a hierarchy device. The only uppercase in the system is the stamp label (and the promo-code field, where the data itself is uppercase).

rules.name: The Whole Cell Rule
rules.body: The catalog grid uses `auto-fill` with a fixed minimum so a card is never cropped or orphaned at any width; the grid grows by whole cells.

rules.name: The Paper Not Depth Rule
rules.body: A surface is distinguished by its ground (paper, slip, tint) and its 1px edge, never by a drop shadow or a gradient. If an element seems to need lifting, give it a brass edge instead.

rules.name: The Two Rules Rule
rules.body: Ruled lines appear in exactly two places: under a table header and above a total (1px brass-300 on screen, 1px ink on the printed slip). Rows are separated by spacing, never by lines.

dos: Do set every panel, card, dialog and input as a white slip with a 1px brass-300 edge and the 0.375rem slip corner on gold paper.
Do use only the two sizes, 0.9375rem compact and 1.75rem display, and rank by weight (400 / 600 / 700) inside them.
Do put every amount in the one money column (7rem, right-aligned, tabular) and format it with `thb()`; describe gold with `describeGold()`.
Do colour prices bold brass-800 and actions white-on-brass-700, hover brass-800.
Do show the live rate stamp on every selling screen, strike it onto the receipt when the rate locks, and print the same stamp.
Do keep the ground flat: rules only under a table header and above a total, the dashed brass-500 perforation above a receipt footer, nothing else ruled.
Do use standard controls (`<button>`, `<input>`, native number and text inputs) at 40px minimum, 44px for icon squares and inputs, 48–56px on the selling path.
Do keep line-height 1.6 on compact text and Noto Sans Thai in the stack; label widths must survive Thai strings.
donts: Don't add a `box-shadow`, a gradient, a blur or a lift on hover anywhere; a surface that needs distinction gets a ground change or a brass edge.
Don't add a third font size, a clamp, or a system display face; the wordmark is the same Noto Sans at display size.
Don't use uppercase, letter-spacing or a kicker as hierarchy; the stamp label is the only uppercase word.
Don't label a value twice; if the receipt shows the total, the panel beside it does not repeat it on counter widths.
Don't use stamp red for anything but the rate stamp and errors, green for anything but success and change, or Thai QR Navy outside the PromptPay header.
Don't draw lines between rows in a list, receipt or table.
Don't replace the Lucide outline set with glyph or emoji icons; the category emoji are shop data, not iconography.
Don't invent a logo mark, shop name or Thai copy; the typographic AGIS wordmark stands until a mark exists.

Don't fill a destructive button red; Delete and Sign out are the red outline (1px stamp stroke, stamp-tint hover) beside a secondary alternative, and a deletion asks first in a `role="alertdialog"` slip.
